ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, points $D$, $E$, and $F$ are located on the three sides respectively, $E$ is the midpoint of $AC$, $AD$, $BE$, $CF$ intersect at point $G$, $BD=2DC$, ${S}_{\triangle GEC}=3$, ${S}_{\triangle GDC}=4$, then what is the area of $\triangle ABC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} $BD=2DC$,\\
$\therefore {S}_{\triangle ABD}=2{S}_{\triangle ACD}$,\\
$\therefore {S}_{\triangle ABC}=3{S}_{\triangle ACD}$,\\
$\because E$ is the midpoint of $AC$,\\
$\therefore {S}_{\triangle AGE}={S}_{\triangle CGE}$,\\
Also, $\because {S}_{\triangle GEC}=3$, ${S}_{\triangle GDC}=4$,\\
$\therefore {S}_{\triangle ACD}={S}_{\triangle AGE}+{S}_{\triangle CGE}+{S}_{\triangle CGD}=3+3+4=10$,\\
$\therefore {S}_{\triangle ABC}=3{S}_{\triangle ACD}=3\times 10=\boxed{30}$.

Since EC = 1 and [GEC] = 3, the perpendicular distance from G to AC is h = 6 in absolute value. Because D is on line AG, write D = lambda G, with lambda > 1 since the diagram shows D beyond G on ray AG. Compute [GDC] using coordinates; with C = (2,0), G = (u,6), D = (lambda u, 6 lambda), the determinant gives [GDC] = 6(lambda - 1) = 4, so lambda = 5/3. Thus the distance of D from AC is 6 lambda = 10. With AC = 2, [ACD] = (1/2)(2)(10) = 10. Finally, BD = 2DC implies [ABC] = 3[ACD] = 30.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, points $D$, $E$, and $F$ are located on the three sides respectively, $E$ is the midpoint of $AC$, and $AD$, $BE$, $CF$ intersect at point $G$. If $BD=2DC$, ${S}_{\triangle GEC}=3$, and ${S}_{\triangle GDC}=4$, then what is the area of $\triangle ABC$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} $BD=2DC$,\\
$\therefore {S}_{\triangle ABD}=2{S}_{\triangle ACD}$,\\
$\therefore {S}_{\triangle ABC}=3{S}_{\triangle ACD}$,\\
$\because E$ is the midpoint of $AC$,\\
$\therefore {S}_{\triangle AGE}={S}_{\triangle CGE}$,\\
Also, $\because {S}_{\triangle GEC}=3$, ${S}_{\triangle GDC}=4$,\\
$\therefore {S}_{\triangle ACD}={S}_{\triangle AGE}+{S}_{\triangle CGE}+{S}_{\triangle CGD}=3+3+4=10$,\\
$\therefore {S}_{\triangle ABC}=3{S}_{\triangle ACD}=3\times 10=\boxed{30}$
